title: Controlled Failover Test — Customer Comms Templates (Status Page + Support Macros + Escalation Guidance)
author: Dev Patel
body:
## Purpose
This page contains approved external-facing language and internal guidance for **controlled regional failover tests** (a.k.a. “game days”) for Redwood Inference.

These templates are designed to:
- Set correct customer expectations without over-promising.
- Reduce Support/CS load with consistent messaging.
- Provide clear escalation paths when customers report impact.

**Principle:** During controlled tests, we communicate like an incident (clear, factual, time-bounded), even if impact is expected and low-risk.

---

## Audience
- **Incident Commander (IC)** and **Comms Lead** for controlled failover tests
- **Support/CS** responders and escalation engineers
- **SRE / Platform** on-call (for validation and customer-impact triage)

---

## When to use these templates
Use these templates whenever we intentionally trigger or simulate failover behavior in staging or production, including:
- Progressive failover of a low-risk slice (e.g., specific routes/models or customer tiers)
- DNS/edge routing changes for validation
- Synthetic impairment tests that may affect latency/streaming stability

Do **not** use these templates for:
- Unplanned outages or degradations (use standard incident comms)
- Customer-specific maintenance windows (use customer maintenance templates)

---

## Guardrails (must-follow)
1) **Never promise SLA improvements** or “no impact.” Use “may” language.
2) **Do not disclose sensitive implementation details** (specific regions, capacity numbers, vendor dependencies, exact thresholds).
3) **Do not provide precise “fix ETA” language** during tests; provide a time window and commit to updates.
4) If unexpected impact exceeds stop conditions, **switch to incident mode** and use standard incident comms.
5) If a customer asks “Did I get failed over?” we can confirm **traffic may have been routed differently** during the window, but avoid detailed routing policy descriptions.

---

## Variables to fill in (copy/paste checklist)
When posting externally, fill these in:
- [WINDOW_START_LOCAL] / [WINDOW_END_LOCAL] (include timezone)
- [WINDOW_START_UTC] / [WINDOW_END_UTC]
- [SCOPE] (e.g., “a small subset of traffic”, “limited set of routes/models”, “low-risk segment”)
- [POTENTIAL_SYMPTOMS] (select from list below)
- [CUSTOMER_ACTION] (usually “no action required”)
- [NEXT_UPDATE_TIME] (or “we will update if we observe unexpected customer impact”)

Approved symptom language (choose only what applies):
- Brief increase in latency
- Intermittent timeouts / 5xx errors
- Short-lived connection resets
- Streaming responses may disconnect and require retry
- Temporary routing to an alternate region

---

## Status Page Templates

### A) Planned Maintenance (preferred when we can pre-announce)
**Use when:** The test is scheduled and we can provide advance notice.

**Title:** Planned Maintenance: Controlled resiliency test (regional failover)

**Body (initial):**
We will be performing a **controlled resiliency test** during **[WINDOW_START_LOCAL]–[WINDOW_END_LOCAL]** ([WINDOW_START_UTC]–[WINDOW_END_UTC]) to validate automated regional failover behavior.

**Scope:** [SCOPE].

During this window, customers **may** experience: [POTENTIAL_SYMPTOMS].

**Customer action:** [CUSTOMER_ACTION].

We will complete the test within the maintenance window and will post an update if we observe unexpected customer impact.

**Component(s):** API / Inference (select appropriate product components)

**Update (completion):**
The controlled resiliency test has completed. Service is operating normally. If you experienced issues during the window and continue to see errors, please contact Support with request IDs and timestamps.


### B) Incident-type Post (use when we do not pre-announce, or impact is visible)
**Use when:** We started the test without prior public maintenance notice, or we observe measurable impact.

**Title:** Investigating: Elevated errors/latency during resiliency test window

**Body (initial):**
We are investigating reports of **elevated errors and/or latency** impacting a subset of requests. This coincides with a **controlled resiliency test** intended to validate automated regional failover behavior.

**Scope:** [SCOPE].

Customers may experience: [POTENTIAL_SYMPTOMS].

We will provide an update by **[NEXT_UPDATE_TIME]** or sooner if conditions change.

**Update (mitigation):**
We have paused or rolled back the test changes and are monitoring recovery. Customers should see improvement as routing stabilizes.

**Update (resolved):**
The issue is resolved and service is operating normally. We are reviewing test results and will incorporate learnings into reliability improvements.


### C) Short “Heads up” Status Page Note (minimal, low-risk window)
**Use when:** Very small scope and no expected customer-visible symptoms, but we want a public breadcrumb.

**Title:** Info: Controlled resiliency test in progress

**Body:**
We are running a short, controlled resiliency test during **[WINDOW_START_LOCAL]–[WINDOW_END_LOCAL]** to validate automated failover behavior for a small subset of traffic. Some customers may observe brief changes in latency or routing. No action is required.

---

## Support Macros (Helpdesk / Email / Chat)

### 1) General macro — “Controlled failover test (informational)”
**When to use:** Customer reports intermittent impact matching expected symptoms during the test window.

**Macro:**
Thanks for reporting this. During **[WINDOW_START_LOCAL]–[WINDOW_END_LOCAL]** ([WINDOW_START_UTC]–[WINDOW_END_UTC]), Redwood is conducting a **controlled resiliency test** to validate automated regional failover behavior for a small subset of traffic.

As part of this test, you may see **brief increases in latency**, **intermittent timeouts/5xx**, or **streaming disconnects requiring retry**.

If you are still seeing issues outside the window, please share:
- Approximate timestamps (with timezone)
- Request IDs / correlation IDs
- Impacted model/route and region (if applicable)

We’re monitoring closely and will escalate if we see unexpected impact.


### 2) Macro — “Customer asks: should I change anything?”
**Macro:**
No action is required on your side. If you have retry logic enabled for transient errors/timeouts, that’s sufficient. If you can share request IDs and timestamps, we can confirm whether the errors aligned with the test window and validate recovery.


### 3) Macro — “Customer asks: was my traffic failed over?”
**Macro:**
During the test window, a subset of traffic may have been routed differently as part of validating automated failover behavior. If you share request IDs and timestamps, we can investigate whether your requests were affected and confirm current service status.


### 4) Macro — “Unexpected severity / impact appears larger than described”
**When to use:** Customer reports sustained impact, broad outage-like symptoms, or SLA-risk.

**Macro:**
Thanks — this sounds outside the expected scope of our controlled test. We are escalating internally now.

If possible, please provide:
- Time range of impact
- Representative request IDs
- Error codes and any client/network logs
- Whether the impact is ongoing

We’ll follow up as soon as we have more details.

(Internal: escalate immediately per the guidance below.)


### 5) Macro — “Dedicated customer concerns (data isolation / traffic routing)”
**Macro:**
For Dedicated deployments, our controlled resiliency tests are designed to maintain isolation and follow agreed routing policies for your service tier. You may observe brief latency or transient errors during the test window, but we do not change data access controls or security posture as part of these tests.

If you share timestamps and request IDs, we can investigate the observed behavior and confirm current status.


### 6) Macro — “Private deployment customer asks about applicability”
**Macro:**
Private deployments vary by configuration. In general, controlled failover tests described on our public status page apply to Redwood-managed hosted services. If you’re running a Private deployment and observed impact, please share details and we’ll route to the appropriate engineering team to confirm whether any shared dependencies were involved.

---

## Internal Escalation Guidance (Support/CS)

### What customers may see (typical)
During controlled failover tests, customer-visible symptoms can include:
- Short bursts of elevated p95/p99 latency
- Increased rate of 429/5xx due to protective load shedding
- Timeouts where clients have aggressive timeouts (<10s) and a retry is needed
- Streaming disconnects when network paths change

### What is NOT expected (escalate immediately)
Escalate to SRE/IC immediately if any of the following are reported or observed:
- Sustained >10 minutes of elevated 5xx affecting broad traffic (not just a low-risk slice)
- Authentication/authorization failures (401/403) correlated with the window
- Data integrity concerns (wrong tenant, wrong output attribution, billing anomalies)
- Cross-region latency spikes that persist after rollback
- Dedicated customer reporting isolation/throughput issues outside the agreed test scope

### How to escalate (Support/CS checklist)
1) Confirm whether the report time falls within **[WINDOW_START_UTC]–[WINDOW_END_UTC]**.
2) Check status page and internal incident channel for current state.
3) Gather the minimum diagnostic bundle:
   - 3–10 request IDs
   - timestamps (UTC preferred)
   - affected endpoint (chat/completions/embeddings) + model name
   - error codes + client timeout settings (if known)
4) Escalate in Slack:
   - If an incident channel exists: post in **#incidents** and tag IC/Comms Lead.
   - Otherwise: notify **#eng-oncall** with “Controlled failover test – unexpected customer impact”.
5) Create/attach a Support ticket and link it in the escalation thread.

**Owner for comms decisions during the window:** IC + Comms Lead (per game day plan). Support should not independently update the public status page.

---

## Comms Roles (who does what)
- **IC (Incident Commander):** decides whether to proceed/pause/rollback; approves external messaging.
- **Comms Lead:** posts status page updates and internal announcement updates; maintains consistency.
- **Support/CS Lead on duty:** monitors inbound, applies macros, escalates unexpected issues.

---

## Pre-test customer outreach (Enterprise / named accounts)
**Use when:** An enterprise account has previously escalated on multi-region resiliency or has strict change expectations.

**Channel:** email from CSM or Support Escalation lead; coordinate with Comms Lead.

**Template:**
Subject: Notice: controlled resiliency test window for Redwood hosted services

Hi [CUSTOMER_NAME],

We wanted to provide a heads-up that Redwood will be running a **controlled resiliency test** during **[WINDOW_START_LOCAL]–[WINDOW_END_LOCAL]** ([WINDOW_START_UTC]–[WINDOW_END_UTC]). The goal is to validate automated regional failover behavior and improve reliability.

**Scope:** [SCOPE].

During the window, you **may** observe brief increases in latency, intermittent timeouts/5xx errors, or streaming disconnects requiring retry. No action is required.

If you notice issues that persist outside the window, please reply with timestamps and request IDs and we will investigate.

Best regards,
[NAME]
Customer Success / Support

---

## Post-test follow-up (optional, for escalated customers)
**Use when:** The customer opened a ticket or asked for confirmation.

**Template:**
Subject: Follow-up: resiliency test completed

Hi [CUSTOMER_NAME],

The controlled resiliency test window has completed and service is operating normally. We reviewed the timeframe you shared and [CONFIRMATION: aligned with the window / did not align with the window].

If you are still seeing issues, please share additional request IDs and timestamps and we will continue investigating.

Best,
[NAME]

---

## FAQs (internal)

**Q: Should we call this “failover” publicly?**
A: Prefer “controlled resiliency test” in customer-facing channels. “Failover” can be used in parentheses if needed for clarity, but avoid implying a customer was “moved” or that a region “failed.”

**Q: Can we tell customers which regions were involved?**
A: No by default. Only share region specifics if Comms Lead + IC explicitly approve (rare; usually unnecessary).

**Q: A customer asks whether this affects billing or usage.**
A: Standard answer: no planned billing changes; usage reflects actual requests processed. If there are concerns about retries causing extra tokens, escalate to Support Escalation lead to coordinate a case-by-case review.

**Q: When do we stop using these templates and switch to incident comms?**
A: When impact exceeds stop conditions or is unexpected in scope/duration. IC makes the call; Support should escalate quickly if reports indicate this.

---

## Internal-only notes (do not copy externally)
- Controlled tests should be linked to the game day plan and runbook in the incident channel.
- Keep a running list of customer reports with request IDs and severity to inform post-test analysis.
- If we roll back, ensure status page includes a clear “paused/rolled back and monitoring recovery” update.

(End of document.)
